messages:
sasha: quick q — noticed weird behavior when using stop sequences + low max_tokens. sometimes the response keeps a token past the stop or returns null logprobs. repro below, can someone confirm what the API contract should guarantee? cc @ken @maria

sasha: repro (trimmed):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
  -d '{\n    "model": "open-llm-7b",\n    "prompt": "Q: Say hi then STOP\nA:",\n    "max_tokens": 2,\n    "stop": ["STOP"],\n    "temperature": 0.7,\n    "top_p": 0.9,\n    "logprobs": 5\n  }'
```

sample response we saw (simplified):
```json
{\n  "id": "res_123",\n  "choices": [\n    {\n      "text": " hi\n",\n      "index": 0,\n      "logprobs": null,\n      "finish_reason": "max_tokens"\n    }\n  ]\n}\n```

sasha: expectation: if stop sequence matches, finish_reason should be "stop_sequence" and text should not include the stop marker. also would expect logprobs when requested unless impossible.

ken: thanks for the repro. short answer: current runtime treats max_tokens as a hard generation cap and stop matching as a post-process step. that means: if the model generates up to the cap before the stop token is emitted, finish_reason=="max_tokens" and we may trim text client-side. logprobs computation is tricky because we compute token-level scores during generation; if we trim across token boundaries (stop matched mid-token or trimmed out) we currently null out logprobs to avoid mismatches.

maria: that's useful context. two follow-ups: 1) do we want to change the contract so stop matching has priority over max_tokens (i.e., allow generating extra token only to detect the stop), or 2) keep hard cap and expose clearer fields so clients can tell why truncation happened?

ken: option 1 is risky — letting generators exceed max_tokens breaks billing guarantees and SLOs. option 2 seems safer: explicitly expose a "stopped_reason" and a boolean like "truncated_by_max_tokens". also document that logprobs may be null when truncation or token-splitting occurs.

maria: agreed. proposal: API guarantees generated_tokens <= max_tokens. Add fields on each choice: "finish_reason" (existing), plus "stop_match": string|null (which stop matched), and "truncated": "none" | "max_tokens" | "post_process_stop" — short list so clients can programmatically handle. Update docs and add a note about when logprobs will be omitted.

ken: implementation notes for runtime: we can 1) keep generation cap as-is, 2) emit stop matching info from post-process step, and 3) if we have to trim tokens out of the middle of a token or drop tokens required to satisfy stop semantics, set logprobs to null and add a reason field. I'll open a PR to runtime to add the metadata and a small test.

maria: i'll update the API spec and dev docs once ken's PR lands. also adding an example response in docs showing both cases (stop_match and max_tokens).

devx-bot: test added: ci/integration/genparams/stop_vs_max — failing on current runtime: https://ci.redwood.ai/12345 (details in PR comment) :construction:

ken: thanks — PR incoming (runtime): https://github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/789 (will include integration test + new choice fields).

maria: pinging @eng-releases for docs rollout once the PR merges.

release-bot: docs deploy scheduled to staging for 2026-03-18 02:15 UTC (staging.redwood.ai/docs) — will include new fields after merge.

sasha: awesome, thanks both. small ask: can we add a short note in the SDKs about how to handle null logprobs? i can add sample code in python/js once docs land.

ken: yes — i'll add a note in the PR templating and add a unit test demonstrating correct behavior for logprobs null vs populated.

maria: follow-up tasks:
- ken: runtime PR + unit tests (ETA: EOD today)
- devx: CI test fix (assigned)
- maria: docs + SDK snippets after merge
- sasha: add a small customer-facing example for the support KB

sasha: thanks — will check back after PR merge. :thumbsup:
